title: CP-5 Driver SPI v1 (SPI 1.0)
description: Machine-readable part of the driver SPI (connection point CP-5): the data a driver receives and returns ($defs) and its members (x-flex-spi). Normative text: the module docstring of flexengine2/drivers/base.py; prose summary: api/cp5-driver-spi.md. tests/api/test_driver_spi_contract.py checks that x-flex-spi equals the Driver class of base.py and that the dataclasses carry exactly these fields. Additive only within v1: a new optional member (UM-4: resources, logs), a new optional field, a new supervise event; anything else is SPI 2.0.

profile.description: the workload profile this driver executes (CP-1 DriverProfile); a driver sets a real value, never '?'

name.description: the implementation (docker, podman, process, systemd, arduino-app-cli, ...); never '?'

exclusive.description: the executor runs at most max_deployments deployments per device

reboots_on_apply.description: apply/remove may reboot the device (os-rauc); additive in 1.0

repairs_digest_drift.description: supervise re-applies a committed workload that runs another digest

runtime.description: FE-4: the x-flex-runtime value this instance serves, None without runtimes

required.plan: (self, current: Workload | None, desired: Workload | None) -> list[str]
required.apply: (self, current: Workload | None, desired: Workload) -> None

optional.stage: (self, current: Workload | None, desired: Workload) -> None
optional.logs: (self, dep_id: str, cursor: str | None, limit: int) -> dict

errors.DriverError: the only exception apply, remove, stage, start, stop, commit and build raise
errors.BuildTimeout: a DriverError: the build ran longer than its timeout (FE-BLD-002)

Workload.description: Driver input: the verified, executor-ready description of one release revision, built by the reconciler from CP-1 and the verified release (CP-3/CP-4). Persisted in state.json (journal) as this object (Workload.to_dict).

digest.description: release manifest digest: the identity of what runs

payload_path.description: verified payload in the engine's content-addressed store

health.description: the signed descriptor's health probe (CP-1 descriptor)

build.description: FE-4: the on-device build of this workload, {} when it was not built on the device

Observed.description: Driver output of status() and list(): what the executor runs for one deployment.

present.description: False only for an unknown deployment, never for an unreachable executor

SuperviseEvent.description: One element of supervise(): local supervision the driver did this tick. Driver-specific extra keys (result, status, slot, version) are allowed.

willRestartAt.description: unix seconds of the next start (exited)

BuildRequest.description: FE-4 driver input of build(): one on-device build (the callable emit is not part of the data).

source_path.description: verified source payload (tar.gz) in the engine's store

spec.description: the signed descriptor's build (command, output, dockerfile, timeoutSeconds)

work_dir.description: a directory of this build the driver may use

digest.description: resultDigest: what the build produced (image id, sha256 of the payload)

DeploymentResources.description: UM-4 driver output of resources(): what one deployment's workload uses now (several containers or processes: their sum). Every key optional; a deployment the driver cannot measure is left out of the answer.

cpuPercent.description: CPU use since the previous sample, 100 = one CPU fully busy (above 100 on several CPUs)

memoryBytes.description: memory in use (container: the runtime's usage; process: resident set; systemd: MemoryCurrent of the unit)

memoryLimitBytes.description: the workload's memory limit (container runtimes: the host's memory when none is set)

WorkloadLogLine.description: UM-4: one line the workload wrote.

msg.description: the line, without its line end

stream.description: absent when the executor does not tell them apart (the journal)

t.description: unix seconds the executor recorded; absent: the engine stamps the time it collected the line

container.description: the container of a multi-container workload (compose)

WorkloadLogBatch.description: UM-4 driver output of logs(dep_id, cursor, limit): lines after the cursor, oldest first, at most limit (the newest when more wait), and the cursor to continue from (opaque to the engine, kept across restarts).

dropped.description: lines skipped because more than limit were waiting

CapabilitiesFragment.description: Driver output of capabilities(): always profile and driver; an exclusive driver adds the placement fragment. The full per-profile fragments are CP-2 (capabilities.v1alpha1 $defs).
